schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center prospective study, SMC NB-2009, replacing total-body irradiation with iodine-131 MIBG in tandem high-dose chemotherapy and autologous transplantation for high-risk neuroblastoma.

schema.label: Induction
schema.text: Nine alternating cycles of CEDC and ICE at 4-week intervals. CEDC: cisplatin 60 mg/m2 on day 0, etoposide 100 mg/m2 on days 2 and 5, doxorubicin 30 mg/m2 on day 2, and cyclophosphamide 30 mg/kg on days 3 and 4. ICE: the table prints ifosfamide as 1 200 mg/m2/day on days 0 to 4, carboplatin 400 mg/m2 on days 0 and 1, and etoposide 100 mg/m2 on days 0 to 4. Doses are reduced by age under 24 months. Surgery is usually after six cycles. Stem cells are collected after cycle 7.

schema.label: Tandem transplant
schema.text: First regimen, CEC: carboplatin, etoposide, and cyclophosphamide, each as printed in the chemotherapy table, on days -7 to -2. Second regimen for metastatic MIBG-avid tumors: iodine-131 MIBG 18 or 12 mCi/kg on day -21, then thiotepa 200 mg/m2 on days -6 to -4 and melphalan 60 mg/m2 on days -3 and -2. Localized or nonavid tumors omit MIBG and use thiotepa 300 mg/m2 on days -6 to -4 with the same melphalan.

schema.label: After transplant
schema.text: Local radiotherapy to the primary site about 6 weeks after the second transplant: 15 Gy at 1.5 Gy for a complete resection, or 21.6 Gy or 30.6 Gy at 1.8 Gy for an incomplete resection, according to residual MIBG or PET uptake. Metastatic sites are not irradiated. Starting about 9 weeks after the second transplant, 13-cis-retinoic acid 125 mg/m2/day for 14 days every 4 weeks and interleukin-2 2 million U/m2/day subcutaneously for 5 days every 4 weeks, until 1 year after the second transplant.

brief.schema_source: Lee et al., Journal of Hematology & Oncology 2017 (PMID 28511709). The full text was read.

publications.title: Local consolidative therapy versus maintenance therapy or observation for patients with oligometastatic non-small-cell lung cancer without progression after first-line systemic therapy: a multicentre, randomised, controlled, phase 2 study.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter randomized phase 2 trial of local consolidative therapy for oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer that has not progressed after front-line systemic therapy. Primary endpoint is progression-free survival. The plan was 94 randomized patients, with an interim analysis at 44 events.

schema.label: Balance
schema.text: Open-label randomization was balanced dynamically on number of disease sites (0 to 1 versus 2 to 3), response to first-line therapy (stable disease versus partial response), central nervous system metastases, intrathoracic nodal status (N0 or N1 versus N2 or N3), and EGFR or ALK status.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Local consolidative therapy with or without maintenance, versus maintenance or observation. Local therapy is surgery, radiotherapy, or both, with intent to ablate all residual primary, nodal, and metastatic disease. Dose and fractionation are chosen by the treating radiation oncologist. Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy, intermediate hypofractionation (the paper gives 15 fractions to the mediastinum as an example), and concurrent chemoradiation are allowed. No single protocol dose is prescribed.

arms.label: Local consolidative therapy
arms.text: Ablation of all residual disease, then maintenance or observation at the physician's discretion.

arms.label: Maintenance or observation
arms.text: Observation is surveillance without cytotoxic therapy. Recommended maintenance options include pemetrexed, bevacizumab for non-squamous disease, erlotinib, crizotinib for ALK rearrangement, and observation. Crossover to local therapy is allowed at progression.

brief.schema_source: Gomez et al., The Lancet. Oncology 2016 (PMID 27789196). The full text was read.
eligibility: Pathologically confirmed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer, AJCC 7th edition, age 18 or older, ECOG 0 to 2, and at most 3 metastases after front-line therapy, not counting the primary tumor.

Front-line therapy is at least 4 cycles of a platinum doublet, or at least 3 months of an EGFR inhibitor for an EGFR mutation, or at least 3 months of crizotinib for an ALK rearrangement. Bevacizumab is not allowed within 2 weeks before radiotherapy.

Lesions are counted after front-line therapy. Lesions that are no longer visible or are no longer avid are not counted. Thoracic nodes from N1 to N3, including supraclavicular fossae, count as one lesion. Immediate local therapy for central nervous system lesions is allowed before randomization, and those treated lesions still count.

A complete response with nothing left to ablate is not eligible. Malignant pleural effusion or uncontrolled third-space fluid is excluded, as is uncontrolled angina, arrhythmia, or congestive heart failure. Metachronous metastases are not expressly excluded.

Recommended, not required, laboratories within 3 weeks: neutrophils at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, white cells at least 3,000/mm3, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, bilirubin at most 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, and alkaline phosphatase, AST, and ALT at most 2.5 times the upper limit, or 5 times if liver metastases are present.

followup.window: Every 6 weeks, plus or minus 2 weeks, for the first year, then at physician discretion
followup.note: CT or PET/CT. Brain MRI or CT if intracranial metastases were present. Progression uses RECIST.

schema.text: Multicenter prospective phase 2 study of adjuvant radiotherapy after radical cystectomy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer. Planned accrual is 76. schema.text: VMAT, 50 Gy in 25 fractions to pelvic nodes, and to the bladder bed only if the surgical margin is positive. The investigators focus on the 2-year PFS as the primary outcome.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: The trial plans to enroll patients with stage T4N1and T1-4N2-3 (AJCC 9th) locoregionally-advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LANPC). Patients will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive 3 cycles of induction chemotherapy with gemcitabine and cisplatin and concurrent cisplatin-radiation or the same regimen plus QL1706 in induction chemotherapy and adjuvant chemotherapy. All patients will receive intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT). QL1706 will begin on day 1 of induction chemotherapy and continue every 3 weeks for 3 cycles in induction therapy and for 9 cycles in adjuvant therapy.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: This is a an open-label, non-inferiority, multicenter, randomized phase III trial aimed to explore the efficacy and safety of shrinking the anterior border of CTV2 in nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients without tumor invasion into the posterior nasal aperture. The enrolled patients will be 1:1 randomly assigned to receive reduced CTV delineation radiotherapy (anterior border of CTV2 defined as 5 mm anterior to the choanae), or standard CTV delineation radiotherapy (anterior border of CTV2 defined as the posterior 1/3 of the nasal cavity).

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: Radiotherapy is the main treatment for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Currently, the 5-year local control rate for NPC is 80% to 85% . However, some patients inevitably experience local recurrence. For early recurrent tumors, salvage surgery can achieve satisfactory tumor control and improve the quality of life for patients, thus being a reasonable treatment option. However, many recurrent tumors are too advanced to be resected. For these unresectable tumors, high-dose re-irradiation is the only potentially curative method.
